New Projects: (in recommended priority order) • Campus Accessibility–This project, would provide dedicated resources to improve campus access to persons with disabilities.
Projects include restroom improvements, exterior pedestrian improvements, and discrete building improvements such as elevator modernizations.
URI has 80 elevators.
Of these, 19 are more than 30 years old and only 18 are newer than 10 years.
Many of our buildings are served by single units.
The combination of single units and aged equipment often results i n downtime and limits access.
This level of support would allow for the modernization of 2 -3 units per year or the replacement of one.
Funding source is RICAP -$16.5MM (FY26/27 @ $3MM FY28-30 @ $3.5MM each year) • Building Envelope Improvements–Many of the campus buildings have envelopes, including roofing systems, that are far past their serviceable life.
With water intrusion active in many locations, protecting these facilities from the damage that this causes and ensuring that environmental conditions remain safe for occupancy, this project addresses critical concerns now present on campus.

Funding source is RICAP -$53MM over 4 years • Carothers HVAC Replacement–The initial core structure of the Library was constructed in 1965 and renovated in two supplemental phases in the early ‘90s.
The current structure is 252,792 gross square feet on five floors with 175 assignable spaces.
Many air handling units are original to the building, have well exceeded their expected 30 -year lifetime, and are in relatively poor condition which can adversely affect air quality.
Funding source is RICAP -$64.3MM starting in FY26 • Campus Access Control–Current evaluation of a university-wide Access Control systems is underway.
In order to provide a safer campus environment, there will be a need to update the software and hardware systems to allow for a secure campus and quick responses to emergencies such as lockdown for an active shooter event.
Total Project Cost and Schedule TBD.
Funding source is RICAP -$1.5MM (just FY26) for initial conversion to a uniform system for the campus.
Future support will be needed to tie in all buildings to this centralized system over time.
Future support level TBD

Funding source is RIHEBC in FY26 • Automotive & Administrative Services–To complete the creation of the new housing district on the western edge of campus and provide proper working space for Automotive and Mail & Printing Services, this project builds an addition to the Central Warehouse for Mail/Printing and provides a new Automotive repair building that replaces the current Automotive building that was once an animal barn. Funding source is RIHEBC -$14.4MM in FY27 • NBC Shoreline Stabilization-The Bay Campus has seen significant shoreline erosion over the past 6 months as storms have intensified and hit the area directly adjacent to Pier Road, our only accessway to the new Pier. Having already contracted with the Army Corp of Engineers, URI is looking at possible ways to secure this area so that this critical roadway is not undermined and taken out of service. We expect that this current study will result in a $6.4MM Total Project Cost that is 35% funded with RI state funding (RICAP) ($2.24MM) and 65% federal sources ($4.16MM) • Water Tower–Built in 1971, the current water tower requires refurbishment, which will be supported by one of the Utility RIHEBC bonds. In addition, additional water capacity is needed to support the expanding campus footprint and fire compliance needs. Recommend building new tower after refurbishing existing tower. The colleges are encouraged to address these inconsistencies asap.
Motion: No approval required.
The Senate is asked to accept the report as editorial.

Faculty Senate Executive Committee Bill #2026-2027-01 October 15, 2026 Faculty Senate Meeting - FOR ACTION (Introduced at the September 17, 2026 Faculty Senate Meeting) Creates standard process for committee formation Approved by FSEC 08/31/26 and 10/7/26 (as amended) Reviewed by CBUM 09/28/26 and 10/8/26 (as amended) Legislation effective date: Spring semester 2027 Rationale: The limited number of faculty senators, in combination with University-Manual-mandated committee staffing requirements, can make it difficult to staff an expanding number of standing committees.
This makes it important to ensure that additional standing committees and subcommittees, whose charges and memberships are proscribed in the University Manual, are created only in response to a significant and sustained need.
In contrast, special committees can be created by the Faculty Senate to address pressing issues.
While there is no limit to the length of time a special committee can exist, the faculty senate must vote to reauthorize each special committee each year.

This legislation mandates that a newly formed committee must exist as a special committee for at least three (3) years before legislation reconstituting it as a standing committee or subcommittee can be considered by the Faculty Senate.
Such legislation must be accompanied by language specifying the charge and membership of the standing committee for inclusion in the University Manual.
This change provides time for the Faculty Senate to 1) consider whether a new standing committee or subcommittee is truly warranted; and 2) craft an appropriate and achievable charge for the body.
This legislation does not mandate that a special committee must be reconstituted as a standing committee after three years.
It is also not retroactive, i.e., all existing standing committees and subcommittees remain unchanged.
This original version of this legislation was introduced for discussion at the 9/17/26 Faculty Senate meeting.
The final version has been revised as follows in response to faculty/staff comments. 1.
Remove language mentioning joint committees .
Joint committees are, by definition, created in concert with the administration (staffing, wording, charge, power balance).
